selectionBoundary: Candidates are experiment graphs, not product or genre selections.
Every admitted candidate cites external motif recurrence and at least one local strong/structural claim.
UNKNOWN couplings are intentionally limited to one or two central questions.
PriorityScore is a retrieval heuristic only; status and kill conditions remain authoritative.
R1 candidates remain historical and are not silently promoted.

candidates.name: Persistent Authorship with Non-Authoritative Response
unknownCouplings: Does external response deepen the player’s own intent or hijack it into evaluator optimization?
Does persistence make revisions more meaningful by changing later possibilities?
candidates.targetDynamic: A self-authored artifact persists, receives interpretable response, and is revised without converting the audience into a score function.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Extend PGP-I across three rounds: player states intent first, artifact persists, deterministic persona comments qualitatively, revision changes one later affordance.
killConditions: players revise mainly to satisfy persona
stated intent disappears after feedback
persistent state does not change a later creative decision

candidates.name: Path-Dependent Automation Architecture
unknownCouplings: Do early architecture commitments create meaningful build identity or merely punish experimentation?
Can automation move attention upward while path dependence still preserves viable redesign?
candidates.targetDynamic: Changing objectives revalue a partially committed automated architecture, creating identity without a universal build.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Symbolic 8-machine micro-factory: 3 objectives, 2 mutually constraining upgrade paths, visible throughput, one limited respec.
killConditions: one opening dominates all objectives
early choice creates unrecoverable lock-in rather than adaptation
automation removes consequential decisions instead of moving them upward

candidates.name: Knowledge-Timed Investigation
unknownCouplings: Does a reset/loop structure make retained knowledge feel like progression, or merely force repetitive traversal?
Does delayed scan information create anticipation and planning, or waiting/friction?
candidates.targetDynamic: Selective evidence acquisition under a bounded cycle creates durable knowledge that changes later routes and decisions.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Extend PGP-D: three short cycles, one action/time budget, one delayed scan, a persistent knowledge journal, and zero inventory unlocks.
killConditions: players repeat traversal without changing their model
persistent knowledge does not alter a later route/action
time pressure produces guessing rather than prioritization

candidates.name: Upstream-Random Buildcraft
unknownCouplings: Does moving randomness from outcome resolution to offer/encounter generation measurably improve attribution and adaptation?
candidates.targetDynamic: Randomness changes the decision problem before choice; player decisions, not hidden post-choice rolls, determine most consequence.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Tiny four-round symbolic draft with matched A/B conditions: random offers/known resolution versus fixed offers/random downstream resolution; identical payoff space.
killConditions: players report equal or worse attribution in upstream-random condition
offer randomness overwhelms build intent
greedy policy performs as well as path-aware policy

candidates.name: Failure-to-Information Mastery
unknownCouplings: Does explicit causal feedback improve learning beyond fast retry alone?
Can assist tuning preserve self-attributed mastery rather than converting success into external rescue?
candidates.targetDynamic: Failure yields a specific model update, immediate retry tests that update, and optional challenge lets the player escalate difficulty voluntarily.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Extend PGP-A with two matched variants: raw instant retry versus retry + one concise causal cue/ghost; add one assist knob that changes timing margin only.
killConditions: causal cue does not change next-attempt behavior
assist users cannot explain what skill improved
harder optional route is solved mainly by route discovery instead of execution

candidates.name: Multi-Timescale Command with Bounded Information
unknownCouplings: Can explicit pause/decision cadence reduce administration burden while preserving crisis pressure?
Do short-term delegated actions create long-term consequence without forcing constant review?
candidates.targetDynamic: Player sets sparse high-leverage intent, recognizable specialists act, and consequences cross tactical/turn/mission timescales while remaining attributable.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Strip existing Station Zero carrier to objective + two doctrine controls + three specialists + pause/commit cadence + one persistent consequence; no new engine/system.
killConditions: configuration/review time exceeds strategic decision time
specialist behavior remains unreadable
long-term outcome cannot be traced to earlier command intent

candidates.name: Rule-Growth Inspection Under Scarcity
unknownCouplings: Does rule growth create procedural mastery or merely memory/reference burden?
Does economic pressure actually change judgment when moral exceptions appear?
candidates.targetDynamic: A stable inspection verb is repeatedly revalued by growing rules while speed, accuracy and exception handling compete for one work budget.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Single-screen document checker: 12 cases over three rounds, add one rule per round, finite clock/pay, two morally salient exceptions.
killConditions: error rate rises without evidence of a learned routine
players rely entirely on external checklist rather than internal model
moral cases do not alter behavior relative to neutral cases

candidates.name: Conditional Ownership / Bank-or-Continue
unknownCouplings: Does making acquired value unbanked until exit create meaningful push-your-luck decisions or simple risk aversion?
What information about future risk is necessary before extraction choice becomes strategic?
candidates.targetDynamic: Acquired value increases both capability/reward and exposure; leaving converts carried value into persistent ownership, so exit timing becomes a decision.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Abstract graph run: 5 nodes, known route-risk bands, loot increases score/value, extraction available after node 2, death loses carried but not banked value.
killConditions: most players always extract at first opportunity
optimal policy is trivial across states
loss feels arbitrary because future risk was not legible

candidates.name: Failure Generates Future State
unknownCouplings: Can failure-generated content feel consequential without making failure strategically preferable?
Does interpretation of failure preserve agency or merely add commentary?
candidates.targetDynamic: A failed action produces a new state/information path that changes later choices instead of forcing reset, while success remains meaningfully distinct.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Text-only 10-node scenario with matched success/failure branches converging later; failure reveals one new fact but incurs one persistent cost.
killConditions: players intentionally fail because failure branch dominates value
success/failure converge without changing later choice
narrative reaction is noticed but not decision-relevant

candidates.name: Communication Topology as Gameplay
unknownCouplings: Does splitting information create mutual agency or merely clerical translation?
What minimum shared vocabulary prevents ambiguity from dominating reasoning?
candidates.targetDynamic: Two players own non-substitutable information and must construct a shared state quickly enough to act.
candidates.cheapestFalsifier: Two-browser micro-task: one player sees world state, one sees transformation rules; 8 short cases with controlled vocabulary/no free shared screen.
killConditions: one role can solve nearly everything alone
communication cost dominates the actual decision
failures are mostly vocabulary ambiguity rather than coordination strategy

executionReason: Wave A maximizes heterogeneity and information gain while reusing existing PGP carriers where possible; upstream-random buildcraft is new but exceptionally cheap. No product/G0 selection follows from any result.
